meta.title: Unit 6 — Prepositions (Test 9)
meta.subject: English Grammar
meta.description: Learn and use common location prepositions to describe positions.

questions.question: The cat is ___ the bag. (The cat is inside the bag)
questions.explanation: "in" means inside. The cat is inside the bag.

questions.question: The book is ___ the car. (The book is resting on the flat surface of the car)
questions.explanation: "on" means on top of. The book is resting on top of the car.

questions.question: "Under" means something is directly above another thing.
questions.explanation: "Under" means below or beneath something, not above it.

questions.question: "Behind" means something is at the back of another thing.
questions.explanation: Yes! "Behind" means at the back of something.

questions.question: Where is the dog if it is 'next to' the box?
questions.explanation: "next to" means at the side of or beside the box.

questions.question: In the sentence 'The apple is in the basket,' the preposition is 'basket'.
questions.explanation: "basket" is a noun. The preposition is "in" because it shows the location relationship.

questions.question: The bird is sleeping ___ the sofa. (Hint: The bird is resting below the sofa)
questions.explanation: We use "under" to show that the bird is below or beneath the sofa.

questions.question: My school bag is ___ the door. (Hint: It is beside the door - 2 words)
questions.explanation: We use "next to" to show that the bag is beside the door.

questions.question: Sort each word — is it a Preposition or an Other Word?
questions.explanation: Prepositions tell us location (in, on, under, behind, between). Other words are verbs, nouns, or adjectives.

questions.question: Sort each word — is it a Preposition or a Verb?
questions.explanation: Prepositions show position relationships. Verbs show action (run, jump, swim, eat).

questions.question: The teacher stands ___ the whiteboard to write. (She is facing it, in front)
questions.explanation: "in front of" is correct because the teacher stands at the front side of the whiteboard.

questions.question: The mouse is hiding ___ two big boxes.
questions.explanation: We use "between" when an object is in the middle of two other things.

questions.question: If you stand 'in front of' the door, you are at the back of the door.
questions.explanation: "in front of" means at the forward or front part, not the back.

questions.question: Which sentence is correct?
options: The dog is next the chair.
The dog is next to the chair.
The dog is next at the chair.
The dog is next in the chair.
questions.explanation: The preposition is "next to". It must include the word "to" to be correct.

questions.question: Arrange the words to form a correct sentence:
questions.explanation: Correct sentence: "The cat is in the bag."

questions.question: Arrange the words to form a correct sentence:
questions.explanation: Correct sentence: "The dog is under the car."

questions.question: Which sentence uses prepositions correctly?
options: My pencil is on the desk.
My pencil is under of the desk.
My pencil is between the desk.
My pencil is in front the desk.
questions.explanation: "on the desk" is correct. "under" doesn't need "of", "between" needs two things, and "in front" needs "of".

questions.question: The rabbit is hiding ___ the big tree. (Hint: The tree blocks the rabbit from view at the back)
questions.explanation: "behind" is correct because the tree block the rabbit from view at the back.

questions.question: He stands ___ the door. (Hint: He is facing the door at the front side of it - 3 words)
questions.explanation: "in front of" is correct because he stands at the forward side of the door.

questions.question: Arrange the words to form a correct sentence:
questions.explanation: Correct sentence: "The ball is between two boxes."
